title: Global and local complete intersections over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. For $g\in S$ let $S_g$ be the localization of $S$ at the multiplicative subset $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; for a ring $T$ let $\dim T$ be the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (1) $S$ is a *global complete intersection over $k$* if $S=0$, or if there are integers $n,c\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\cong S$ such that $\dim S=n-c$. (2) $S$ is a *local complete intersection over $k$* if there is a family $(g_i)_{i\in J}$ of elements of $S$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_{i\in J}D(g_i)$, $D(g)=\{\mathfrak q:g\notin\mathfrak q\}$, and each $S_{g_i}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition 00S9 (label definition-lci-field, line 35817), including the convention that the zero ring is a global complete intersection
